qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Pearson VUE and UK qualification awarding bodies (Edexcel) operate as secure testing and certification toll booths, but 5-year median GAAP Return on Capital/ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~10.3% (7.9% in 2021 to 11.3% in 2025, failing the >=12% Munger threshold). Furthermore, higher education courseware and learning content face long-term pricing compression and generative AI disintermediation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). While Pearson VUE computer-based testing and accredited examinations provide a strong testing toll booth, Pearson's 5-year median GAAP Return on Capital/ROIC is sub-hurdle at ~10.3% (consistently below 12% across 2021-2025), burdened by historical intangible asset acquisitions. Learning content also faces persistent pricing headwind from generative AI automation.
qualitative.evidence: Global learning and assessment provider generating ~£3.5-3.8B in revenue with adjusted operating margins improving from 11.2% in 2021 to ~17% in 2024-2025. Reported Return on Capital was 7.9% (2021), 8.7% (2022), 10.3% (2023), 10.5% (2024), and 11.3% (2025), failing the 12% multi-year hurdle required for empirical proof of moat under Gate 3b.
